subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Session Architecture: Shared LLM + Isolated Sessions + Public Knowledge Base

question: Should OpenClaw keep this broad multi-session/shared-knowledge RFC as a core architecture direction, or split the remaining work into narrower session-family, memory-security, and UI issues?
rationale: Current main already implements adjacent primitives, while the remaining shared-memory/RAG and cross-session architecture choices affect product direction, security boundaries, config, storage, plugins, and UI.

options.title: Split And Narrow
options.body: Keep or replace this umbrella with specific maintainer-approved issues for remaining session-family, memory/security, and UI gaps.

options.title: Close As Umbrella Superseded
options.body: Close this issue only if maintainers decide the remaining pieces are fully owned by narrower open items such as topic-session families and WebChat conversation management.

options.title: Sponsor Full RFC
options.body: Adopt the RFC as a maintainer-owned architecture program with a written migration, compatibility, and security plan before implementation.

recommendation.title: Split And Narrow
recommendation.body: Keep or replace this umbrella with specific maintainer-approved issues for remaining session-family, memory/security, and UI gaps.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the narrower session-management tracker and have recent session-area history, making them the best available owner for the product-direction call.
